question: Pankaj purchased two bikes, first for Rs. 24000 and the second for Rs. 20000. He sold both the bikes, first one at the profit of 20 percent and the second at a loss of 30 percent. What is the overall profit or loss?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net Profit/Loss can be calculated directly by finding the profit and loss amounts on the individual items.

⇒ Net value = (20% of 24000) − (30% of 20000)

⇒ Net value = 4800 − 6000 = −1200

Since the net value is negative, it represents an overall loss.

**∴ The correct answer is Loss = ₹1200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

CP of first bike (CP₁) = ₹24000

Profit on first bike = 20%

CP of second bike (CP₂) = ₹20000

Loss on second bike = 30%

**Formula Used:**

Profit = (Profit% ÷ 100) × CP

Loss = (Loss% ÷ 100) × CP

 
 Bike 1 CP = 24000
 
 
 SP = 28800
 
 
• 
 

 +20% (+4800)
 
 
 Bike 2 CP = 20000
 
 
 SP = 14000
 
 
• 
 

 −30% (−6000)
 
 Total Net = +4800 − 6000 = −1200 (Loss)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Profit on first bike = (20 ÷ 100) × 24000 = ₹4800

⇒ Loss on second bike = (30 ÷ 100) × 20000 = ₹6000

⇒ Net value = Profit on first bike − Loss on second bike

⇒ Net value = 4800 − 6000 = −1200

⇒ Since the net amount is negative, there is an overall loss of ₹1200.

**∴ The correct answer is Loss = ₹1200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total CP and Total SP Method

You can also find the overall profit or loss by calculating the sum of all Cost Prices and the sum of all Selling Prices. If Total SP > Total CP, there is an overall profit. If Total SP < Total CP, there is an overall loss.

Selling Price Formula

SP = CP × (100 ± Profit/Loss%) ÷ 100. Use + for profit and − for loss.

Successive Transactions

When an article is sold successively to multiple buyers, the final SP can be calculated by multiplying the original CP with the successive profit or loss multiplying factors respectively.
